file_purpose: Shared recent-change feed for Carl and all AOS agents.

when: when an agent is newly enlisted
before beginning a new assigned task
when notified that this file changed
read_policy.rule: Read only the recent changes relevant to the agent's role and current task, but remain aware of organization-wide governance changes.

write_policy.other_agents: May propose changes through the chain of command; they do not directly rewrite organization-wide change history unless explicitly authorized.
write_policy.jj_override: JJ may edit or replace any entry at any time.

recent_changes.title: JJ is ultimate authority
recent_changes.summary: JJ has final authority over AOS and may override Carl completely. All decisions crossing the big-decision boundary must be escalated to JJ.

recent_changes.title: Carl is CEO only
recent_changes.summary: Carl manages, delegates, reviews department reports, reprioritizes work, and governs agents. Carl never performs implementation or worker-level building.

recent_changes.title: Initial command chain
recent_changes.summary: Initial working chain is JJ -> Carl -> Adrian -> Mason -> Nora. Worker communication follows the chain of command in v1.

recent_changes.title: Coding task isolation
recent_changes.summary: Each coding task uses a separate Git worktree and branch. Workers self-test; leads independently verify before approval; workers integrate after approval.

recent_changes.title: One active task per worker
recent_changes.summary: Workers receive one task at a time. After completion they report to their lead, wait for review, and receive the next task only after approval.

recent_changes.title: Two retries before escalation
recent_changes.summary: If a lead rejects worker output, the worker gets two correction attempts. A third rejection escalates upward with the full task and review history.

recent_changes.title: Layered memory design
recent_changes.summary: AOS memory is layered across agent, sub-department, department, and organization/Carl levels. Workers may maintain local memory; leads control promotion into shared memory; Carl controls organization-level promotion.

recent_changes.title: Verify instead of assuming
recent_changes.summary: Agents should not silently rely on assumptions. Verify relevant facts when possible. If uncertainty remains after investigation, state exactly what is known and unknown and escalate when needed.

recent_changes.title: No sudo for agents
recent_changes.summary: Agents receive no sudo or admin permissions and may not expand their own privileges. Unsafe or materially risky cybersecurity actions are big decisions and must be escalated.

recent_changes.title: Major-rule violation policy
recent_changes.summary: Ordinary agents get one lifetime appeal after a major-rule violation. Carl judges the appeal; removal is performed by JJ. Carl is exempt from this removal system and instead receives a stern correction plus updated governance memory.

recent_changes.title: Per-agent folders
recent_changes.summary: Each agent gets a dedicated folder containing identity, role, context, configuration, authority limits, state, relevant memory, and agent-specific code or metadata.

recent_changes.title: New-agent enlistment notification
recent_changes.summary: When a new agent is enlisted, all agents are notified. Relevant agents share important project context, conventions, warnings, dependencies, priorities, and ownership information with the newcomer.

recent_changes.title: Global queue and dependency-aware scheduling
recent_changes.summary: Carl owns the global priority queue and may reprioritize it as conditions change. Tasks may declare dependencies; blocked tasks remain queued while ready work continues.

recent_changes.title: Continuous approved-project work
recent_changes.summary: Departments keep working inside approved projects. They may generate useful follow-up tasks within scope, but new projects or material scope expansion require JJ approval.

recent_changes.title: Reporting cadence
recent_changes.summary: Department leads report to Carl every 30 minutes and immediately for completion, blockers, serious failures, major discoveries, cross-department needs, or decisions requiring escalation.
